judge: Opus 5.5 (fresh adversarial reviewer agent, no prior scores)
rubric: height vs cliff, edge seams, style vs beodeul cliffs, front-elevation look, 1x readability

majors: Front-elevation/1x readability: the 16-row cut body is a near-flat fill of the same packed-earth as the straight track (same mid-brown, only ~1 value darker plus single-pixel speckle and a faint chevron that disappears below 3x). There is no crest highlight at the top row, no toe shadow/lip at the bottom of the face, and no top-to-bottom tonal gradient, and the side cheeks are uniform-width vertical strips rather than wedges, so in probe-1x/3x and the hill-village 4x crops the piece reads as the track passing level through a slot/gap in the cliff, not as a slope climbing up and away.
minors: Left cheek dark brown vs right cheek bright tan strip: both are vertical bands of constant width; acceptable as lit/shaded walls but they add to the 'slot' read.
Speckle (isolated dark single pixels) in the body is noisier than the clustered pebble texture of the native beodeul cliff face.
At rise 1 the cut is only 16 rows of almost-track colour; in probe-1x it is indistinguishable from the track simply continuing.

majors: Stacked ramps (probe2 right, 1 + strip + 2): both flights inherit the flat-fill ramp defect, so the composition reads as a level dirt track crossing two gaps in two cliffs with a strip of track between; no sense of climbing two flights.
minors: Stacked stairs (probe2 middle 2+strip+2, right-middle 1+strip+2) join cleanly: cobble road landing between flights, crest/toe rows align with the native cliff faces, cheeks continuous; these pass as composed art on their own.
At the landing strip the native cliff end-caps beside the cut draw a diagonal return on the left side of the middle stack, which is renderer side, not piece art.

summary: Stairs (8/8) PASS: correct height for every rise (2 treads per level), crest meets the upper road and toe meets the cobble foot, cheeks match the native cliff end-caps, and they read clearly as stairs at 1x in the probes and hill villages; only cosmetic minors (brick-course risers, bright lips, repetition). Ramps (8/8) FAIL on one shared major: the cut body is essentially the flat track fill with speckle, with no crest highlight, toe shadow, gradient or wedge cheeks, so in the real renderer it reads as the track passing level through a slot in the cliff rather than a slope. Heights and seams of the ramps are otherwise correct. Stacked stairs compose well; stacked ramps fail for the same reason. Overall FAIL.
